Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and
directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

Background:

On December 16, 2024, staff solicited bids for construction for the Local Streets Rehabilitation
Project No. 7935. The project area is located within City Pavement Management Zones 2, 9,
and 29.

The work scope involves improvements to Asphalt Concrete pavement, cross gutters, curb and
gutters, Americans with Disabilities Act curb ramps, signing, striping, loop detector
replacements, and traffic control.

On January 23, 2025, the City received four bids. Below are the following results:

 Rank  Contractors  Amount
  1  All American Asphalt  $  5,922,140.25
  2  Sully-Miller Contracting Company  $  6,040,000.00

The Engineer’s Estimate for the project is $10,346,770.00.

Staff reviewed the bids, evaluating accuracy, costs, experience, and references. As a result,
staff recommends awarding the project to the apparent lowest responsible and responsive
bidder, All American Asphalt (contractor), based on their pricing and qualifications.

On February 7, 2025, the City advertised a Request For Proposal for construction management
and inspection services for the project. On March 10, 2025, a total of 12 proposals were received
with two of them deemed non-responsive. Below are the list of firms:

result, staff recommend selecting Willdan Engineering to provide construction management and
inspection services for this project.

A construction engineering support services agreement was approved on December 5, 2023
with Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc. (Kimley-Horn), design engineer. Services provided are
clarification/interpretation of construction documents; review and recommend approval of project
required submittals; review and recommendations related to change orders; attend construction
meetings (as needed); conduct a final site visit with the project team to verify completion of the
work.

To date, two contract amendments to the Kimley-Horn Agreement were issued to provide
additional scope of work including utilities investigation, soils boring, design of alley
improvements, and supplemental design revisions subsequent to city pavement value

Case Surveying will be performing centerline monumentation for the convenience of the City. Case Surveying will research

research to identify where protection will occur. Centerline monuments control the centerline of streets and will be located in
the center of intersections, beginning of curves, end of curves, at points of reverse curves, angle points within the centerline
and points of interest between the centerline and a tractor or parcel boundary. Monuments may also be found to control
property corners at the back of walk, in walk, or on top of curb. Four ties are anticipated to be received from the City that
includes lead, tack and tag number placed in the top of curb in the pre-construction survey. Pre-existing ties that a previous
survey has set will also be used. Upon completion of construction, the City will inform the surveyor to reset any lost
monuments in the post construction survey. When monument resets are complete, drafting will prepare the corner record to
document the monument per the Surveyor’s Act Section 8771. It will identify what was found during pre-construction, what
remains at post-construction, and what is set to show the post-construction condition. Upon drafting completion, the
surveyor will process the corner record to the agency having jurisdiction for final review, signing, and filing. Review
comments will be addressed by the surveyor. Final approved corner records will be delivered to the City for reference.

On February 24, 2025, City staff advertised a Notice Inviting Bids for City Project No. 7606,
Potter Street Storm Drain Replacement (Project No. 7606). Project No. 7606 will affect
replacement and realignment of the existing section of storm drain and catch basins located

on a privately owned property at 11701 Potter Street. The project will replace the damaged pipe
and storm drain components, improve the hydraulics and conveyance of captured stormwater at
this location.

Project work scope includes removal, realignment, and replacement/restoration of the existing
City owned storm drain; new catch basins; pavement restoration; and sidewalks and gutters.

Background:

On January 16, 2024 the City approved a Design Build Agreement for the Hermosillo Park
Project. City Parks and Recreation staff in collaboration with Public Services Engineering staff
recommended solicitation and procurement of design and construction of the project using
progressive design build (PDB) to avoid delaying the project schedule and resolve construction
phasing constraints.

PDB is a variation of the Design-Build method, allowing project owners to advertise the request
for qualifications (RFQs) from potential Design-Build Entities earlier in the procurement process
with preliminary design and less defined project scope. Utilizing PDB, project owners can enter
into contract with Design-Build entities on a shorter timeline, reduce procurement cost, and
encourage higher degree of collaboration between project stakeholders resulting in a more
transparent risk allocation between owner, designers, and builders.

The design build agreement for the Hermosillo Park Project was executed on March 12, 2024,
and a project initiation meeting to kick off the project was held on the same day. The design build
team provided 35% design on August 19, 2024 with a preliminary construction cost estimate that
exceeded the project budget. City staff and the design build contractor, Reyes Construction met
on several occasions to reduce the cost of the project through maximizing efficiencies and scope
reduction without impacting the core nature of the project. Reyes Construction provided a 65%
design on November 26, 2024 and a revised Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) for the project
on December 30, 2024. The GMP projected a funding gap of 43% for the project.

SUBJECT: APPROVAL TO PURCHASE MERIDIAN ARCHER 1200 BARRIERS

Background:

In recent years, the threat of terrorism, particularly vehicle-ramming incidents, along with
concerns about crowd control and traffic accidents, has underscored the urgent need for rapid-
deployable, high-performance perimeter security solutions. Therefore, ensuring the safety of
pedestrians and personnel at public events, street closures, parades, and busy civic activities is
a top priority for the City.

The Meridian Archer 1200 Barrier is a portable steel structure well-suited to meet the City’s
needs. Unlike traditional concrete or water-filled barriers, the Archer 1200 is non-electric and
requires no heavy equipment for deployment. This barrier can be quickly placed, repositioned,
or removed by City staff with minimal training, making it ideal for temporary use at changing
event locations. Acquiring this equipment supports the City’s Public Safety mission by enhancing
operational readiness and responsiveness. With the increasing number of community events
and a focus on pedestrian safety, these barriers provide the flexibility, durability, and reliability
needed in urban security planning. Their modular design allows for scalable deployment, offering
a customizable solution for venues of all sizes.

Furthermore, Meridian Rapid Defense Group is the sole manufacturer and distributor of the
Archer 1200 system, and no other product matches its tested performance and patented
portability. Due to its proprietary nature, this procurement qualifies as a sole source purchase.
Purchasing these barriers is a proactive investment in public safety, aligning with the City’s
strategic goals to safeguard residents, visitors, and staff while maintaining an open and
welcoming community.

Subject:  Sole Source Justification for the Purchase of Meridian Archer 1200 Barriers

  The purpose of this memorandum is to justify the sole source purchase of
  Meridian Archer 1200 Barriers. These barriers are essential for ensuring
  enhanced public safety and security for large public events, crowd control,
  vehicle mitigation, and similar activities. After conducting thorough research, it
  has been determined that Meridian Archer 1200 Barriers are the only product
  meeting the operational requirements necessary for our application.

  The Meridian Archer 1200 Barrier is a mobile, modular, and rapidly deployable
  security solution designed to mitigate vehicle threats in high-risk environments.
  The barriers are engineered to meet stringent safety standards and offer the
  following advantages:
  • Certified and tested to ASTM and PAS 68 standards for hostile vehicle
  mitigation.
  • Rapidly deployable and easily reconfigurable without the need for heavy
  equipment or permanent installations.
  • Provides non-lethal, passive security without impeding pedestrian access.
  • Fully modular system allowing for customized configurations based on
  security needs.
  • Requires minimal maintenance and operational oversight.

  The purchase of Meridian Archer 1200 Barriers as a sole source acquisition is
  justified based on the following criteria:

  •  Unique Features & Performance: The Meridian Archer 1200 Barriers
  incorporate proprietary technology and are the only known barriers
  capable of meeting both the Department’s mobility and safety
  requirements. The ability to deploy and reposition the barriers quickly
  without requiring power, hydraulics, or permanent fixtures makes them
  uniquely suited for our operational needs.
  •  Compatibility with Leased Equipment: The City has already deployed
  Meridian Archer 1200 Barriers in past security operations. Acquiring
  additional units ensures seamless integration with existing infrastructure,
   eliminating the need for retraining personnel and modifying operational
  protocols.
  •  Lack of Viable Alternatives: Market research has confirmed that no
  other vendor produces a mobile, modular, and certified vehicle mitigation
  barrier with equivalent performance characteristics. Competing products
  either require permanent installation or rely on electronic/hydraulic
  mechanisms.
  •  Manufacturer is Sole Distributor: Meridian Rapid Defense Group is the
  exclusive manufacturer and distributor of the Archer 1200 Barrier. There
  are no third-party resellers authorized to provide the product, thereby
  eliminating competitive procurement options.

Based on the aforementioned factors, the purchase of Meridian Archer 1200
Barriers as a sole source acquisition is in the best interest of the City. The barriers
provide the most effective, mobile, and temporary solution for vehicle threat
mitigation, ensuring the safety of personnel and the public.

Request:

The Developer is requesting approval of DA No. 2025-0001 to expressly define a development
project’s rules, regulations, commitments, and policies for a specific period of time for the
development of the Specific Plan area. Development Agreements such as this are commonly
known as “Statutory Development Agreements” (SDA). The purpose of an SDA is to “lock in”
entitlement approvals to provide for more certainty in the entitlement process.

Authority:

The Development Agreement Act (California Government Code §65864 et seq.)
authorizes cities to enter into binding development agreements with persons having a legal or
equitable interest in real property for the development of such property, all for the purposes
of strengthening the public planning process, encouraging private participation
and comprehensive planning and identifying the economic costs of such development.

Analysis:

Summary of Key Terms of DA No. 2025-0001:
  • Term: 10 years from the Effective Date of this Agreement (the “Term”), with an automatic
  additional five (5) years if certificates of occupancy have been issued for at least 150 total
  Residential Units by the expiration of the initial Term.
  • Subdivision Maps. Any tentative subdivision map or tentative parcel map approved for the
  property after the Effective Date shall automatically be extended for the term of

  magnitude. This provision does not apply to restrict or limit any assignment of
  this Agreement to an Affordable Housing Builder as part of the Transfer of the
  Affordable Parcel to the City or the Affordable Housing Builder.
  • Vested Development Rights. Developer acquires vested right to develop the Project
